floating_artifact.defect_claim: An image reference runs bytes that can change under an unchanged file, so infrastructure drifts to whatever the registry serves.
premises: The cited compose `image:`, Kubernetes container `image:` or Dockerfile `FROM` (a stage that is neither an earlier stage nor scratch) is a reference tools/gates/infra-policy/image-reference.ts judges mutable (PIN_MUTABILITY): a moving or major-only tag, an opaque tag, an implicit latest, a `${VAR:-default}` or unchecked variable, or a malformed reference; a digest and a required `${TAG:?…}` are immutable.

A postgres-family image in a file .github/manifests/postgres-image.json lists as a consumer is judged by tools/gates/postgres-image-manifest.ts instead: the manifest's expected reference is compliant, a divergence is the claim (owner_rule_id manifest_divergence).
Helm values and chart files are read and observed; no owner rules their image maps, so they raise no claim.

privileged_runtime.defect_claim: A container runs with host privilege or as root.
premises: tools/gates/infra-policy/runtime-privilege.ts reports the cited compose service or pod setting as privileged: privileged true, a dangerous capability, a host namespace, a bind of a container runtime socket or a directory above one (paths normalised), privilege escalation, or an unconfined seccomp or AppArmor profile.

Or the runtime user is root: a compose `user:` or pod runAsUser of root/0, or a Dockerfile final stage that sets no USER (unset) or USER root; the WAL-G derivative that .github/manifests/postgres-image.json names is the sanctioned exception and is recorded as an observation.

A bind whose source the owner cannot place (a relative path that climbs out of the project, `~`, `$VAR`), and a runtime user named by a variable (Dockerfile `USER $APP_USER`, compose `user: "${UID}:${GID}"`), is an unresolved observation, not a claim.

literal_secret.defect_claim: A secret literal sits in a file the gitleaks path allowlist hides from the CI secret scan.
premises: The cited compose or Kubernetes env entry matches the aquaculture-env-secret-assignment rule of .gitleaks.toml (regex, keywords, entropy and value allowlists, read by tools/gates/infra-policy/secret-allowlist-premise.ts) and a path allowlist of that rule hides its file.
Only the key, line and the value's length are reported; the value never enters the finding.
With .gitleaks.toml unreadable in the workspace or snapshot, the rule is recorded as unavailable instead of judging.

nats_password_identity.defect_claim: A NATS server configuration authenticates a client by something other than its mTLS certificate CN, which ADR-015 forbids.
premises: tools/gates/infra-policy/nats-identity.ts finds, in an authorization block or an account's users of the parsed config, a password, token or nkey, a user given as a `$VARIABLE`, or a user name that is not a certificate DN.
A commented-out key is not configuration; a credential is located by key and line and its value never enters the finding.

missing_runtime_guard.defect_claim: A Kubernetes workload container runs without a memory limit or without its readiness or liveness probe.
premises: tools/gates/infra-policy/runtime-guards.ts (podGuards) reports the gap for the cited container; init containers and Job/CronJob pods need no probes.

A guard that a kustomize patch supplies to the base is recorded as a composition observation and removed from the claim only when every deployment of the base (each kustomization no other kustomization lists, with the patches of the kustomizations it reaches) supplies it; a patch in an overlay that does not deploy the base supplies nothing.
Compose services are not this rule's surface.

security_header_inheritance_drop.defect_claim: An nginx level sets headers of its own and so serves without headers it would otherwise carry, because add_header does not inherit into a level that declares any.
premises: tools/gates/infra-policy/nginx-header-inheritance.ts (headerLevels) computes the cited level's dropped headers from the parsed configuration.
A level with an include whose headers this run cannot see is recorded as unresolved instead of claimed.

unpinned_terraform_source.defect_claim: A Terraform module source can change content under an unchanged .tf file.
premises: tools/gates/infra-policy/terraform-pins.ts (MODULE_SOURCE_PINNING) judges the module's source unpinned: a git branch or no ref, a registry module without version, or an archive without a go-getter checksum.
A source the owner cannot classify is recorded as unresolved, never counted as pinned.
The source is reported with its userinfo masked and a query value kept only for ref, rev, depth, archive, checksum and filename; a source that is not one string literal is not reported.
